messages.content: Give me a new fictional screening population so I have to rebuild the reasoning myself.

content.text: Try this on your own. Write down your reasoning as you go.

arguments.statement: A fictional university exercise screens 2000 people for an invented condition with 5% prevalence. Sensitivity is 80% and specificity is 95%. Calculate expected true positives, false negatives, false positives, true negatives, and positive predictive value. Does 80% sensitivity imply 80% probability of the condition after a positive result?
arguments.modelSolution: There are 100 people with the condition and 1900 without it. Expected counts are TP = 80, FN = 20, FP = 95, TN = 1805. PPV = 80/(80+95) = 80/175, approximately 45.7%. Sensitivity conditions on disease status, whereas PPV conditions on a positive result. These fictional numbers are not a clinical recommendation.

content.text: Problem posed. The learner's thinking and answer will follow.
